taxonomic_note: Accepted Opuntia rufida (strict species concept). Do not collapse it into O. microdasys or automatically transfer older red-glochid pricklypear records. Source-pool admission does not certify Central Texas nativity.
look_here_first: Look closely at the pad areoles: many dense rust-red to reddish-brown glochid clusters, with ordinary long rigid spines typically absent. Then check the whole branching pad habit; do not use pad color or the red dots alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Deep-review B031: accepted SW Texas to NE Mexico Chihuahuan Desert taxon; no three exact target-zone counties established.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not treat SW Texas state-level records, O. microdasys, or older rufida labels as confirmed target-zone counties.

best_field_traits: Flattened jointed cactus pads with regular areoles
Dense reddish-brown to rusty glochid tufts at the areoles
Ordinary long stiff spines often absent; inspect multiple mature pads
Branching clump of pad segments; pad habit alone is insufficient
Flowers and fruit should be checked when present, but areole/spine structure is the first useful cue
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Distinguish from O. microdasys using expert-confirmed taxon concept, pad/areole distribution, and habitat; its colored glochids alone are not species-proof. Unlike the reviewed strict O. azurea comparison, mature O. rufida usually lacks obvious long rigid spines.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Dense rust-red glochid tufts with few or no ordinary spines favor O. rufida; conspicuously long-spined, bluish-padded plants suggest other Opuntia. Verify against modern identified material rather than historical labels.
